Jensen Huang, the only boss Nvidia has ever had, resigned last week after reports that US intelligence suspected Alice Huang, a Chinese businesswoman he had grown close to, of working for China’s main spy agency. In this video, Patrick Boyle looks at what the Nvidia scandal means for investors: the Megaspeed chip smuggling allegations and the 50,000 chips Nvidia’s own audit couldn’t find, a board that had 33 years to prepare a succession plan and didn’t, and why losing the man who acted as the central bank of the AI boom could matter far more to the stock market than one CEO’s private life. Along the way, I draft a few of the risk factors that Nvidia seems to have left out of its filings.
